title: Bandwidth-aware GPU placement and IaC lifecycle playbook
author: Priya Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook codifies an egress/bandwidth-aware GPU placement strategy and the associated Terraform/IaC lifecycle for Redwood’s multi-tenant inference fleet. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor egress contention, improve tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants, and maintain clear operational procedures for rollout, monitoring, and rollback.

Scope:
- Applies to all GPU clusters managed by the gpu-allocator service in public cloud regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1).
- Covers node labeling, tenant egress tagging, scheduler policy, IaC module variables, CI/CD gating, and runbook actions for hotspots.
- Does NOT change model-level runtime parameters (those are handled by eng-serving-runtime docs).

Context and motivation:
- Observed incidents in 2024 where a small set of tenants with high-embedding workloads saturated node egress links, leading to 99.9th percentile generation latency spikes.
- Existing placement is GPU-count-first; we add a bandwidth signal to avoid co-locating heavy-egress workloads with latency-sensitive customers.

Key components (short):
- tenant-metadata-service: authoritative egress profile for a tenant (low/medium/high).
- gpu-allocator: placement controller that consumes tenant egress profile + node egress capacity annotations.
- egress-sharder: sidecar/proxy for shaping and tagging flows per-tenant for billing/telemetry.
- IaC modules: tf-module/gpu-node-profile and tf-module/egress-pool to manage node pools, tags, and autoscaling policies.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Per-tenant soft egress SLO: 250 Mbps sustained per GPU for "medium" profile, 50 Mbps for "low" profile.
- Node-level saturation alert: sustained >= 80% egress utilization for 60s => P3 alert (investigate).
- Tail-latency objective: 99th percentile generation latency < 450ms for latency-tier customers; placement policy aims to keep node egress headroom >= 30% for those tenants.

Node labeling and tagging conventions:
- node.kubernetes.io/gpu-type = a100|h100|t4
- node.redwood/egress-capacity-mbps = "4000" (example per-node uplink)
- node.redwood/egress-pool = "high-throughput" | "isolation" | "shared"
- Tenants are annotated via tenant-metadata-service with tenant.egress_profile = "low|medium|high". This drives placement decisions.

Placement policy rules (ordered):
1) If tenant.egress_profile == "isolation", place on nodes in egress-pool=isolation (single-tenant node pool).
2) Else prefer nodes where (node.egress_free_mbps - requested_estimated_mbps) >= 30% of node.egress_capacity.
3) When multiple candidates, prefer the node with lowest co-located "high" tenants count.
4) If no node satisfies headroom, route to dedicated burst pool (capacity permitting) or fall back to cross-region placement as configured by routing policy (costly; used as last resort).

Estimating requested_estimated_mbps (simple estimator):
- generate request: token-rate * avg-token-size-bytes * api-overhead-factor -> convert to Mbps.
- Embedding-heavy jobs include an override parameter in the request metadata to help allocator (recommended).

IaC module contract (variables and defaults):
| variable | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| egress_pool_name | string | "shared" | Name for the egress pool attached to node group |
| node_egress_capacity_mbps | number | "4000" | Advertised uplink capacity for node type |
| isolation_max_tenants | number | "1" | Max tenants for isolation pool nodes |
| enable_egress_shaper | bool | "true" | Inject egress sidecar configuration |
| autoscale_min | number | "1" | Min node count |
| autoscale_max | number | "50" | Max node count |

(Represented above as a preformatted table in Confluence - the IaC modules in the repo use these variables.)

CI/CD and gating for IaC changes:
- All changes to tf-module/gpu-node-profile or tf-module/egress-pool must have:
  - an accompanying plan that includes an estimated egress capacity delta and tenant-impact analysis.
  - at least two reviewers from eng-infra and eng-platform (automated reviewer assignment: CODEOWNERS).
  - Canary deployment: promote to a single region small pool (canary pool) behind feature-flag:placement.egress-aware=true.
- Automated tests in the CI pipeline (Buildkite):
  - terraform fmt & validate
  - unit tests for module input validation (go/py tests)
  - integration test: deploy a small cluster in ephemeral sandbox, simulate three tenant profiles and verify scheduler respects headroom constraints.

Rollout playbook (high-level):
1) Create IaC change with new variables set for isolation pools and node annotations.
2) Run CI, deploy to staging region, run integration test harness (see infra/ci-eval).
3) Enable canary pool in us-west1 with 3 nodes; route 5% of matching traffic via feature-flag routing.
4) Observe for 48 hours: target metrics (node egress utilization, 99p latency, tenant error rate).
5) Gradually ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% by region using rollout automation.
6) If any threshold breach occurs (see Rollback criteria), disable feature-flag and revert IaC changes.

Rollback criteria (automated):
- 99p latency for priority tenants increases > 20% over baseline for 30m.
- Node-level network saturation > 95% for 10m.
- Unbounded increase in network error rates (5xx) for any tenant > 1% of requests for 15m.

Operational runbook (responding to an egress hotspot):
1) Detect: Prometheus alert egress_node_sustained_high (>=80% for 5m).
2) Triage: identify top contributors using egress_sharder.flow_breakdown_by_tenant dashboard.
3) Immediate mitigation options (in order):
   a) Evict best-effort pods for non-isolated tenants from affected node: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 <node>
   b) Apply temporary per-tenant shaping via egress-sharder: redwoodctl egress-sharder throttle --tenant=<id> --mbps=100
   c) Scale up isolation/burst node pool (if autoscale_max allows): terraform apply -var="egress_pool_name=burst" -auto-approve
4) If eviction or shaping insufficient, enable cross-region fallback in gpu-allocator config for impacted tenant(s): update placement policy via config map and restart allocator (rolling): kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-allocator
5) Post-incident: run hotspot postmortem, capture tenant patterns, and consider promoting heavy tenants to scheduled isolation pools (owner: capacity team).

Monitoring and dashboards (recommended panels):
- Node egress utilization (per-node, 1m/5m/1h)
- Top-20 tenant egress by node
- 99p generation latency by tenant tier
- Egress sharder drop/shape rates and per-tenant throttles
- IaC drift: desired node annotations vs observed annotations

Prometheus alerts (examples):
- alert: NodeEgressSustainedHigh
  expr: node_network_transmit_bytes_rate{job="node-exporter"} / node.redwood_egress_capacity_mbps > 0.8
  for: 5m
  labels: { severity: "warning" }
- alert: PriorityTenantLatencyRegression
  expr: increase(request_latency_count{priority="high",quantile="0.99"}[30m]) > scalar(0) and (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant)) > 450)
  for: 10m
  labels: { severity: "critical" }

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: capacity@redwood (capacity team)
- Service owner: eng-infra GPU team (oncall: infra-gpu@pagerduty)
- IaC module owner: infra-iac (codeowners: @infra-iac)

Post-incident actions and continuous improvement:
- Add failing tenant patterns to synthetic load tests and CI integration tests.
- Consider quota or surcharge for sustained high egress to encourage tenant migration to isolation pools. Finance and pricing should be consulted before enforcement.

Appendix A — Example terraform snippet (gpu node pool):
```hcl
module "egress_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/tf-module/egress-pool.git"
  name   = "isolation-eu-west1"
  node_egress_capacity_mbps = 10000
  isolation_max_tenants = 1
  autoscale_min = 1
  autoscale_max = 10
}
```

Appendix B — Quick CLI commands:
- throttle tenant: redwoodctl egress-sharder throttle --tenant=tenant_123 --mbps=150
- force drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- restart allocator: kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-allocator -n redwood-infra

Notes and references:
- For full billing/chargeback integration see cloud-accounts-and-networking/egress-billing-clarity-and-multipath-metering-spec.json
- For scheduler internals see eng-infra/team-wiki/gpu-allocator-safety-checklist-and-iac-adapter-guide.json

- 2024-07-15: Drafted by Priya Patel (initial policy, metrics, and IaC contract).
- 2024-11-02: Updated SLOs and added egress-sharder integration (reviewers: Diego Morales).
- 2025-02-10: Finalized rollout playbook, CI gating steps, and example Terraform snippet.
